printers_bundle.briefing:
Kraków, the winter of 1795. The Austrian eagle hangs over the Town Hall, and the Constitution of the Third of May is a thing men whisper. Tonight a printer of the Rynek has two hundred leaves of it, fresh and damp, hidden in the Cloth Hall passage, and he dares not fetch them himself. They must go to Pani Zofia's salon behind the Town Hall door, where the right people will read them before breakfast.

Three roads lie open. The smuggler at the cellar door by St Adalbert's knows where the bundle lies. The passage urchins will fetch anything for a coin, or a promise. Pani Zofia, at the Town Hall door, may lend a stranger an invitation and a cloak, if he gives her reason.

Mind the watch. Mind the grey-coated informer between the Cloth Hall lanterns: slip him a false leaf from behind and he will carry it to the Corporal for you. At ten the curfew bell tolls, and for some minutes after it the Austrians see twice as far.

summary.salon: In a borrowed cloak and with a borrowed smile you walked the bundle through the front door of the Town Hall, past a sentry who bowed you in.
summary.decoy: The informer carried your false leaf to the Corporal, and half the watch spent the small hours freezing at the Florian Gate.

summary.fail_beaten: You fought the watch and lost. They beat you with their musket butts and dragged you to the Town Hall cellars, the very building you were bound for.
summary.fail_bundle: The printer's leaves went into an Austrian stove. The printer himself has left the city by the Florian Gate.

corporals_ledger.title: The Corporal's Ledger

journal.blurb: The watch rota for the winter lies in Corporal Brandt's ledger in the sentry-box by St Mary's. Copy it, or steal it.

corporals_ledger.briefing:
Every hour the watch walks, every post it keeps, every night until the thaw: Corporal Wenzel Brandt writes it in a ledger with a red ribbon, and the ledger sits on a table in the sentry-box by St Mary's, watched by his orderly, Private Novak.

Whoever holds those hours owns the night. Copy the rota and the Austrians will never know what they lost; tear it out and run, and they will change every hour of it by morning, but you will have the one night they don't.

The laundress Marianna, at the drying lines by the Winiarnia, washes the Corporal's shirts. A basket gets a woman into the post. A man can play the drunk: the watch lets a drunk sleep it off where he falls, and the Winiarnia sells the costume by the bottle. Or Novak can simply be paid. The Corporal himself takes his glass at the Winiarnia at half past ten.

The boatman in the alley by St Adalbert's will carry the rota to the river.

salt_barge.title: The Salt Barge

journal.blurb: Forty muskets from the 1794 caches came down the Vistula in salt barrels. The raftsmen want them landed their way; the salt merchants' guild, theirs.
journal.reward_hint: Whoever lands the muskets owns them. The other side will remember.

salt_barge.briefing:
The Vistula quays south-west of the walls, past the Grodzka gate and along the riverside: granaries, wharves, a fish market, salt barges frozen into the ice. On one of them, under a false floor of salt, forty muskets from the caches of 1794 have come down from the Tatra villages.

The raftsmen want them sledged off the quay tonight, their way, and they will keep them. The salt merchants' guild wants them weighed and written into its books as salt, and they will keep them too. Herr Pichler, the Austrian exciseman, sits in his hut on the quay with the barge's manifest and weighs every barrel that moves.

Bartek the raftsman is on the wharf. Master Wierzbięta of the salt merchants is by the fish market. Choose which of them lands the muskets. It is a long walk from the Rynek: out by Szewska and the Grodzka gate, then west along the river.

bishops_letter.title: The Bishop's Letter

journal.blurb: A letter under Bishop Turski's seal leaves for Vienna with the morning post: Church lands for a Te Deum, and three 'Jacobin' priests for the Emperor's prisons.
journal.reward_hint: Return the letter to the old Bishop and he is in your debt. Print it and the Church is shamed.

miracle.blurb: Brother Kajetan the sacristan can make a Madonna weep, for a fee. The whole church will run to see.

bishops_letter.briefing:
Bishop Feliks Turski is old, and ill, and frightened for the Church's lands. His secretary, Canon Wolski, has written a letter in his name to Vienna: a Te Deum for the Emperor, loyalty sworn on the Bishop's seal, and three names of 'Jacobin' parish priests for the Emperor's prisons. It lies in the Bishop's writing case in St Mary's, waiting for the morning post.

Get it before dawn. A woman might borrow a habit from Sister Agnieszka on St Mary's steps; a man might be lent a cassock by Canon Sierakowski, who drew the plans to restore Wawel and has no love for Wolski. Or Brother Kajetan the sacristan, for three złoty, can make the Madonna in the north aisle weep, and every canon in the church will run to see. If anyone has the key to the confessional's second door, Canon Wolski confesses at ten.

Then decide what to do with the letter: give it back to the old Bishop so he knows that you know, or promise it to the printers.

magnates_ball.briefing:
The magnates give a masquerade in the Town Hall, in honour of nobody and in defiance of everybody. Baron von Hauer, the man Commissioner Margelik has sent ahead to govern Kraków until spring, will attend, with Lieutenant von Arnim at his elbow. So will Count Stanisław Wodzicki, thirty-one, who fought with Kościuszko and dances as though he still were.

Make the night count. Blackmail von Hauer, if you hold his debts or his secret; poison his punch, if you have the stomach and a vial; or win Count Wodzicki, and with him the magnates' retainers. Then slip out before the unmasking at midnight.

Pan Kostka, the majordomo at the Town Hall door, admits the well-born, the well-recommended, and tonight, being short of servants, anybody who can carry a tray.

pillory.briefing:
They have raised a second pillory in front of the Town Hall, for the example. In it stands Józef Kmita, seventeen, the old sergeant's grandson, placarded for singing the Mazurek in the Cloth Hall arcades. At eleven the drummer comes, and the flogging. A crowd is gathering, and it is not jeering.

Free him and get him to the boatmen's cellar by St Adalbert's. Wojtek the carter, at the front of the crowd, can turn it into a mob with one word; a riot will empty the pillory and fill the cells. Or keep it quiet: a key from Rózia, or a pick while the guard looks elsewhere. Or ask old Salomea the fortune-teller, by the stocks, what frightens a Moravian soldier. The city's coldest seat has had many occupants. It need not have this one.

kingpin.title: The Kingpin

journal.blurb: Wilk, the river king, owns the Vistula quays: the smuggling, the fences, a third of the red lantern's take, and the Austrians' ear when it pays. Kill him, and the docks are yours.
journal.reward_hint: The district flips whatever the method, but every method leaves a different river behind it.

kingpin.briefing:
Wilk (the Wolf) is the river king. His men own the Vistula quays: every tenth barrel, the fences at the fish market, a third of Mother Weronika's take, and when it pays, the Austrians' ear. He sold two of your raftsmen to the Polizei last month. He will sell you next.

Tonight he makes his round of the quays as he does every night: the warehouse office, cards in the yard behind the fishermen's tavern from a quarter to ten, the steam at the riverside bathhouse at twenty to eleven, his barges under the cargo hook at half past eleven, then a prayer at the riverside shrine. Two bodyguards keep a ring round him, one always looking back. They know faces, and nobody reaches arm's length of Wilk without being searched.

So go the long way round. Poison what he drinks. Rig what he stands under. Set fire to what he owns. Turn his own quay against him; there is even a French mechanic on the riverside who builds a certain machine. Jędrek, his lieutenant, hates him, and may help. When it is done, decide who rules the river, and get out through the Grodzka gate.

lines: Magnifique. It will stand on the quay by the fish market. A machine is only a threat, until it isn't.
Look! The big one has seen it. He is running. Loyalty, it seems, has a limit.
She is ready. We call her the National Razor, but in Polish it sounds less friendly.

success.text: The Vistula docks answer to the movement now: one district of eight.

failure.text: Wilk lives, and he knows your face. He will sell it to the Austrians by Sunday.

poison.text: Poison: the quay blames the fish; the Church does not.

accident.text: An accident with a cargo hook: nobody to hang, nobody to blame.

fire.text: Wilk's warehouse burned with its grain. The guilds count the loss.

riot.text: The raftsmen rose. The garrison marched down to the river and stayed.

guillotine.text: A guillotine on the Vistula quay. The Church and the Salon are appalled; the street is drunk on it; the Austrians impose a curfew sweep.

knife.text: A knife in the dark. The river respects that.

pistol.text: A pistol shot heard across the city. Every Austrian now knows your name.

jedrek_spared.text: Jędrek rules the river for the movement. Half of Wilk's men follow him; the rest went to the Austrians.

jedrek_banished.text: No more kings on the river: the guilds rejoice, and the Underworld splits.
